sources.scope: 2026–2027 regulations, Articles 4.5–4.9, 5.2–5.3 and Appendix I: controlling components, credit, sequence and formal progression.
Programme overview verifies full-time English-language BSc at Venlo, biological and Earth sciences and sustainable food applications.
Programme rationale confirms three named concentrations and applied biology, agriculture and food topics.
Current semester overview verifies four collaborative research projects, design challenge and individual thesis.
Programme future page provides application and graduate examples as search context.

curriculum: Appendix I and Article 4.6 give 60 EC in each year. Year 1 has eight 5 EC courses, four 2.5 EC skills courses, and two 5 EC projects. Year 2 uses the eight course and four skill slots from the Appendix I period lists plus Research Projects III and IV. The illustrated choice takes the first-listed Planetary Systems concentration, and Planetary Boundaries is its required preparation. Article 4.8(2) describes this as a skills course, but Appendix I places all three mandatory concentration preparations in the 5 EC course column, consistent with the separate 5 EC concentration preparation in Article 4.6. Year 3 uses four 5 EC courses, two 2.5 EC skills modules, one 5 EC design challenge and the 30 EC thesis. The table lists two courses and one skills unit in each concentration period. The example assigns skills credit to the third item in each period, consistent with the parallel Agricultural and Food skills labels. The official semester overview cautions that titles may change. No detailed syllabus claims are inferred from module titles.
progression: Articles 4.9 and 5.2 require successful completion of the first-year core courses, skills and projects before concentration modules, and prior participation in the mandatory preparation with attendance met. Concentration registration is due before 1 June of the preceding academic year. Year 2 requires two courses and one skills module in each elective period, with eligibility subject to any catalogue prerequisites. The example selects coherent choices in the correct periods following the full first-year foundation. Article 5.3 requires an approved thesis plan before starting the final 30 EC individual project. The regulations describe no separately credited internship or extra thesis prerequisite within the standard plan.
